summary: Argus is a programming language created at MIT by Barbara Liskov between 1982 and 1988, with Maurice Herlihy, Paul Johnson, Robert Scheifler and William Weihl. It extends the CLU language, uses most of its syntax and semantics, and was designed to support distributed programs.
notableFor: Distributed programs built from guardians and atomic actions

summary: ArkTS is a high-level, general-purpose, multi-paradigm, compiled, declarative, statically typed language developed by Huawei as a superset of TypeScript. It compiles to machine code through the Ark Compiler and was first released on September 30, 2021, on OpenHarmony.
notableFor: Huawei language for HarmonyOS development

summary: AssemblyScript is a TypeScript-based programming language that is statically compiled to WebAssembly. It resembles ECMAScript and JavaScript but adds static data types, and it is developed by the AssemblyScript Project and its community.
notableFor: TypeScript-based language compiled to WebAssembly

summary: ATS is a multi-paradigm, general-purpose, high-level functional programming language designed by Hongwei Xi as a dialect of ML. It combines theorem proving with practical programming through advanced type systems.
notableFor: Combines theorem proving with practical programming

summary: AutoHotkey (AHK) is a free, open-source custom scripting language for Microsoft Windows. It is designed for keyboard shortcuts, macro creation and automating repetitive tasks in Windows applications.
notableFor: Keyboard shortcuts and automation on Windows

summary: AutoIt is a freeware programming language for Microsoft Windows. It was first intended for creating automation scripts for Windows programs and has since grown to include enhancements in language design and functionality.
notableFor: Freeware Windows automation language

summary: AutoLISP is a dialect of Lisp built specifically for the full version of AutoCAD and its derivatives, such as AutoCAD Civil 3D and AutoCAD Mechanical. Its API and interpreter are not included in the AutoCAD LT product line.
notableFor: Lisp dialect for AutoCAD

summary: Averest is a synchronous programming language and a set of tools to specify, verify and implement reactive systems. Its tools include a compiler for synchronous programs, a symbolic model checker, and a tool for hardware and software synthesis.
notableFor: Tools for verifying reactive systems

summary: AWK is a scripting language designed for text processing and typically used as a data extraction and reporting tool. Like sed and grep, it is a filter and a standard feature of most Unix-like operating systems.
notableFor: Standard Unix text-processing filter language

summary: Axum is a domain-specific concurrent programming language based on the Actor model, under active development by Microsoft between 2009 and 2011. It is an object-oriented language for the .NET Common Language Runtime with C-like syntax.
notableFor: Actor-model concurrency on .NET

summary: B is a programming language developed at Bell Labs circa 1969 by Ken Thompson and Dennis Ritchie. It is classified on Wikipedia as a procedural programming language.
Ballerina is a general-purpose programming language designed by WSO2 for cloud computing application software. It is free and open-source software released under the Apache License 2.0.
notableFor: Cloud application language from WSO2

summary: BASIC is a family of general-purpose, high-level programming languages designed for ease of use. The original version was created by John G. Kemeny and Thomas E. Kurtz at Dartmouth College in 1964 so that students in non-scientific fields could use computers.
notableFor: Created at Dartmouth College in 1964 for ease of use

summary: A batch file is a script file for DOS, OS/2 and Microsoft Windows. It is a plain text file of commands run by the command-line interpreter and can use conditional branching and looping constructs such as IF, FOR and GOTO.
notableFor: Command-line script files for DOS and Windows

summary: bc is an arbitrary-precision mathematical calculator program with an input language similar to C. It supports both interactive command-line use and script processing.
notableFor: Arbitrary-precision calculator with C-like input

summary: BCPL is a procedural, imperative and structured programming language first implemented by Martin Richards at the University of Cambridge in 1967. It was originally intended for writing compilers, and its stripped-down successor B was the basis of the C language.
notableFor: Its successor B was the basis of C

summary: BeanShell is a small, free, embeddable Java source interpreter with object-oriented scripting features, written in Java. It runs on the Java virtual machine and extends standard Java syntax with conveniences such as loose types and method closures.
notableFor: Embeddable Java source interpreter

summary: BETA is a pure object-oriented language that originated in the Scandinavian School of object-orientation, where the first object-oriented language, Simula, was developed. It introduced nested classes and unified classes with procedures into patterns.
notableFor: Unified classes and procedures into patterns

summary: BLISS is a system programming language developed at Carnegie Mellon University by W. A. Wulf, D. B. Russell and A. N. Habermann around 1970. It was perhaps the best known system language until C became common a few years later.
notableFor: Well-known system language before C

summary: Blockly is a client-side JavaScript library for creating block-based visual programming languages and editors. A Google project released under the Apache License 2.0, it typically runs in a web browser.
notableFor: Google's block-based visual programming library

summary: BlooP is a simple, Turing-incomplete programming language designed by Douglas Hofstadter to illustrate a point in Gödel, Escher, Bach. Its main control structure is a bounded loop, so all programs terminate and it can express only primitive recursive functions.
notableFor: Turing-incomplete language from Gödel, Escher, Bach

summary: Boo is an object-oriented, statically typed, general-purpose programming language for the Common Language Infrastructure. It uses Python-inspired syntax and focuses on language and compiler extensibility, with features such as type inference, generators and macros.
notableFor: Python-inspired syntax on the Common Language Infrastructure

summary: Boomerang is a programming language for writing lenses, which are well-behaved bidirectional transformations. Those lenses operate on ad-hoc, textual data formats.
notableFor: Bidirectional transformations (lenses) for text data

summary: Bosque is a free, open-source programming language designed and developed by Microsoft. It was inspired by the syntax and data types of TypeScript and the semantics of ML and Node/JavaScript, with goals of better software quality and developer productivity.
notableFor: Microsoft language inspired by TypeScript and ML

summary: The C shell is a Unix shell created by Bill Joy while he was a graduate student at the University of California, Berkeley in the late 1970s. It was widely distributed from the 2BSD release of the Berkeley Software Distribution, which Joy first distributed in 1978.
notableFor: Unix shell created by Bill Joy

summary: C* is a data-parallel superset of ANSI C with synchronous semantics. The Wikipedia summary gives no further detail on its design.

C-- is a C-like programming language designed to be generated mainly by compilers for high-level languages rather than written by human programmers. It was created by functional programming researchers Simon Peyton Jones and Norman Ramsey, and it is represented in plain ASCII text rather than bytecode.
notableFor: Compiler-generated intermediate language in plain ASCII

summary: C/AL was the programming language used within C/SIDE, the client/server integrated development environment in Microsoft Dynamics NAV and Dynamics 365 Business Central up until version 14. It is a database-specific language that resembles Pascal and has been replaced by AL.
notableFor: Language of Dynamics NAV, replaced by AL

summary: Caché ObjectScript is part of the Caché database system sold by InterSystems. It is a functional superset of the ANSI-standard MUMPS language and adds object-oriented programming, a macro preprocessor and embedded SQL.
notableFor: Superset of MUMPS in the Caché database system

summary: Calcpad is free and open-source mathematical software created by Nedelcho Ganchovski in 2014. It is designed for engineering calculations and documenting results as HTML, PDF or Microsoft Word reports, using its own simplified syntax.
notableFor: Engineering calculation notes with simplified syntax

summary: Caml is a multi-paradigm, general-purpose, high-level functional programming language and a dialect of the ML family. It was developed in France at INRIA and the École normale supérieure in Paris.
notableFor: ML dialect developed at INRIA

summary: Carbon is an experimental programming language designed for interoperability with C++, started as an open-source project at Google. Chandler Carruth introduced it at the CppNorth conference in July 2022 as a successor to C++, and its experimental MVP version 0.1 is expected in late 2026 at the earliest.
notableFor: Experimental C++ successor from Google

summary: Catrobat is a block-based visual programming language and open-source non-profit project. It was first released in 2010 by Wolfgang Slany of Graz University of Technology in Austria, and it lets teenagers create games, animations and apps directly on a smartphone.
notableFor: Block-based smartphone app creation for teenagers

summary: Cecil is a pure object-oriented programming language developed by Craig Chambers at the University of Washington in 1992 as part of the Vortex project. It has similarities to Objective-C, Modula-3 and Self, and its goals were extensibility, orthogonality, efficiency and ease of use.
notableFor: Pure object-oriented language from the Vortex project

summary: CEEMAC is a programming language developed in the 1980s for the Apple II family of computers. It was developed by Brooke Boering and published by Vagabondo Enterprises.
notableFor: Language for Apple II computers

summary: CESIL (Computer Education in Schools Instructional Language) is a programming language designed to introduce pupils in British secondary schools to elementary programming. It is a simple language containing a total of fourteen instructions.
notableFor: Teaching language for British secondary schools

summary: Ceylon was an object-oriented, strongly statically typed programming language with an emphasis on immutability, created by Red Hat. It ran on the Java virtual machine and could be compiled to JavaScript, with a design focused on readability, predictability and modularity.
notableFor: Red Hat language emphasizing immutability

summary: CFEngine is a configuration management system written by Mark Burgess. Its primary function is automated configuration and maintenance of large-scale computer systems, including servers, desktops and embedded network devices.
notableFor: Configuration management system by Mark Burgess
